column2: Automatic Prefix Caching (design doc)
column8: the freed blocks are added to the tail of the free queue in the reverse order
column9: vLLM evicts prefix-cached blocks from one LRU free queue; sha256 is default block hash since v0.11; per-request salt is offered to block timing attacks on content.
column10: Salt only partitions hash namespace; the free queue and eviction order are global, so a tenant's allocations still evict another tenant's cached blocks (eviction-contention channel untouched).
column11: High: core mechanism for eviction-based prefix-cache attacks; single shared LRU is the attack surface the advisor named.

column2: Security (Prefix Cache Timing Side-Channel Mitigation; multi-tenant isolation)
column8: Options such as `cache_salt` reduce specific cross-tenant risks, but they are not an isolation boundary.
column9: vLLM officially states it gives no tenant isolation inside one process; cache_salt is opt-in, secret, and only mixed into the first block hash; recommends a dedicated instance per tenant.
column10: Doc does not quantify residual channels (eviction, preemption, memory pressure, batch interference) and offers no shared-pool partitioning.
column11: High: maintainers concede the gap; a measured residual channel under salting would be directly relevant upstream.

column2: [RFC]: Cache Salting for Secure and Flexible Prefix Caching in vLLM (#16016)

column11: High: defines the threat model upstream accepted, so anything outside it is a candidate gap.

column2: [Core] Prevent side-channel attacks via cache salting (#17045)
column8: When present, the salt is injected into the hash of the first block, ensuring that only requests with the same salt can share cached blocks.
column9: Merged 2025-04-30; implements single-barrier salt in the first block hash.
column10: Does not change allocator, free queue, or eviction; salted and unsalted blocks still compete for the same pool.
column11: High: baseline defense any eviction-channel attack must defeat.

column11: Medium: closed integrity path; useful as history and to frame poisoning via other key-construction bugs.
